Quality-of-Earnings Takeaways
  • Heavy Fab Reinvestment: CapEx absorbed $10,216.0M as Intel aggressive builds out 18A fabs in Ohio and Oregon, consuming 77.5% of operating cash flow.
  • Positive True FCF: Despite massive capital deployment, True FCF remained positive at +$1,074.0M after accounting for all $1,894.0M in employee SBC.
  • $23B Equity Infusion: Intel completed a $23B public equity offering during the quarter, bolstering balance sheet liquidity to sustain IDM 2.0 commitments.
Row 4: Operational Execution Audit & Earnings Call Forensic Q&A Highlights
WINS / DRAGS AUDIT
Operational Wins (What Management Did Right)
1. DCAI Revenue Explosion ($7,330M): Data center revenue surged +77.9% YoY, driven by enterprise server refresh cycles and Oracle Cloud Xeon adoptions.
2. Massive Top-Line Beat ($16,513M): Net revenue shattered the $14,000M consensus hurdle by +$2,513M (+17.95%), achieving the largest dollar surprise in years.
3. Non-GAAP Gross Margin Lift (43.0%): Beat prior guidance by +500 bps as high server utilization minimized idle fab charges.
4. Balance Sheet Fortification: Successfully closed a $23B equity offering to preserve investment-grade credit rating during peak fab buildout.
Execution Drags (What Went Wrong / Headwinds)
1. Q4 Gross Margin Collapse (38.0%): Guided down -500 bps sequentially as external TSMC packaging costs on Lunar Lake erode client profitability.
2. Violent -23.00% Stock Sell-Off: Stock crashed from $92.07 to $70.89 after-hours, destroying $112B in market value as Q4 EPS was guided to $0.25.
3. Client PC Sequential Digestion: CCPG revenue fell -5.0% YoY to $8,085M as enterprise OEMs digested inventory ahead of Windows 10 refresh cycles.
4. Intel Foundry Cash Burn: Internal eliminations expanded to -$6.3B, highlighting the protracted timeline before foundry reaches independent cash breakeven.
Institutional Conference Call Analyst Q&A Highlights & Critical Analyst Questions
C.J. Muse (Cantor Fitzgerald) Q4 Gross Margin Compression & Lunar Lake Tile Cost Structure

Question: Why is Q4 gross margin stepping down 500 bps from 43% to 38% despite higher full-year revenue volumes, and how much of that is driven by external TSMC packaging costs on Lunar Lake?

Executive Answer: David Zinsner (CFO) admitted that Lunar Lake’s architecture relies on external foundry packaging which carries lower initial gross margins until Panther Lake brings high-volume compute tiles back to internal 18A fabs in 2027. Q4 also bears elevated start-up costs for Fab 34 and Fab 52.

Timothy Arcuri (UBS) Client PC Inventory Digestion & AI PC Momentum

Question: Can you unpack the Client Computing guidance drop to $15B-$16B? Are enterprise customers delaying corporate desktop refreshes until Windows 10 end-of-life in late 2027?

Executive Answer: Pat Gelsinger (CEO) explained that after aggressive pre-ordering in Q3, OEM customers in North America and EMEA are maintaining lean inventory. While AI PC adoption is expanding rapidly with over 100M Core Ultra units targeted by year-end, component supply chains remain disciplined.

Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein Research) Intel Foundry External Commitments & 18A Milestones

Question: Where do customer tape-outs stand on 18A, and how much external cash burn should we expect from Intel Foundry before breakeven in 2028?

Executive Answer: Pat Gelsinger reiterated that 18A is on track for full manufacturing readiness, with Panther Lake and Clearwater Forest leading internal production. Commercial foundry pipeline stands at over $15B in lifetime deal value, with major hyperscaler tape-outs scheduled for H1 2027.
